scraped.title: Effective School Guidance Counselling Workforce
scraped.subtitle: Supporting the development of an effective school guidance counselling workforce in West Bank and Gaza schools
scraped.description: In the West Bank and Gaza, young people face growing challenges when it comes to preparing for life after school, whether it's pursuing higher education or entering the workforce. To help them make informed decisions about their future, our project supports the Palestinian…
body: In the West Bank and Gaza, young people face growing challenges when it comes to preparing for life after school, whether it's pursuing higher education or entering the workforce. To help them make informed decisions about their future, our project supports the Palestinian Ministry of Education in building a stronger, more inclusive school guidance system for students in grades 9 to 12.

This World Bank initiative is part of a broader education reform program aimed at improving student outcomes and opening new pathways to university, vocational training, and employment. ICON’s project supports national and international goals, aligning with the Palestinian Authority’s education strategies and global efforts like the Sustainable Development Goals. It aims at empowering Palestinian youth through better career guidance and psycho-social counselling at school. Our focus lies in transforming how schools support students' academic, career, and emotional development and wellbeing – ensuring no one is left behind.

We are working hand-in-hand with local educators, decision-makers, and ministry staff to: Strengthen school counselling systems by developing a clear framework, job profiles, and tools that define the role and responsibilities of guidance counsellors. Equip educators with the right skills through tailored training programs that improve how career counselling and psycho-social support are delivered in schools. Create opportunities for girls in STEM by supporting girls’ secondary schools with targeted, gender-sensitive interventions like mentoring, family engagement, and campaigns to break down education biases. Connect schools to the labour market by identifying ways to better align education with labour market needs—including the use of mobile technology and online platforms for career resources, mentoring, and job-matching.
